lines: When is everyone free? Find the evening, then plan it.
The Schedule tab opens on Time off: a row for each member, a column for each day, Off, Tentative or Working.
The event's days carry its label, and each day counts who is off.
Add my time off sets your own week, a day at a time.
Save, and your row fills in, for everyone, without a reload.
This week shows the next seven evenings, and how many are free on each.
On Wednesday, everyone's free from seven thirty.
A timeline from noon to midnight shows who works when, and says it in words for a screen reader.
My hours takes your own working hours, up to two stretches a day, on the quarter hour.
Plan dinner in chat opens the Everyone thread with a draft, ready to send, not sent.
On an evening someone works, it asks those who are free instead.
The Popkin home names the next evening everyone is free.
The Host sets the event from Popkin settings: a label, a first day and a last day.

lines.text: On a phone, the table scrolls inside the screen, the names fixed.
From ten twenty-four pixels, the headline and its chat action sit side by side.

lines: Schedules has a switch. While it is off, the tab is gone and its screens say so. Nothing is lost.
What no screen shows: each member changes only their own row, and a wrapped-up Popkin's schedule is read only.
An open screen follows every change, live.
That is journey twenty-two. Popkin is a platform for pop-up communities.
